intro: Resource paths often need lexical normalization before lookup. A stack resolves dot segments while preserving ordinary segment names and their order.
task: Resolve dot and dot-dot path segments while rejecting traversal above the root.
requirements: Use relative slash-separated paths only: reject a leading slash, backslash, colon, or NUL anywhere. Ignore empty segments and .; resolve .. by removing one prior segment, rejecting traversal above root. Return remaining segments joined with /; an empty result is valid.
Text inputs contain valid Unicode scalar characters and at most 10000 characters.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Treat segments as a stack; .. removes the most recent normal segment.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Reject an attempted pop from an empty stack instead of quietly discarding it.

explanation: Resource paths often need lexical normalization before lookup. A stack resolves dot segments while preserving ordinary segment names and their order.
This is a lexical resource-name exercise, not a filesystem security check. It does not resolve symlinks, percent escapes, or operating-system path aliases.
